label: Move 0 failure modes
query: What are the six failure modes that usually stall Kyriba rollouts, and how should AbarVa de-risk them for Lakeshore?
answer: For Lakeshore specifically, the Kyriba risk isn’t the core platform — it’s how it lands in your existing finance/IT operating model. Pattern-matching from Kyriba and peer TMS rollouts, there are six failure modes I’d plan against, and how AbarVa should counter each: 1) Fuzzy business case — no CFO‑visible value spine Failure mode: Kyriba gets framed as “modern treasury tooling,” not a P&L lever, so scope drifts and exec attention wanes after go‑live. De‑risk with AbarVa: (1) Lock a value tree before design: working capital (days liquidity, cash visibility), bank fee reduction, FX slippage, manual effort takeout. (2) Attach each Kyriba module / phase to 1–2 explicit KPIs with owners (e.g., “cash position accuracy to 99% by T+0, owned by Treasurer”). (3) Bake those KPIs into the Move 0 charter for LSH‑KYRIBA‑TREASURY‑2026 so later scope debates are objective (“does this change move these numbers?”). 2) Weak data and bank-connectivity spine Failure mode: Underestimating work to normalize bank statements, map cash hierarchies, and stabilize SFTP/API connections. Result: “Kyriba is wrong” because feeds are wrong. De‑risk with AbarVa: (1) Treat bank connectivity and data quality as a pre‑Move, not a line item — a dedicated workstream with cutover criteria: % of accounts connected, reconciliation error rate, feed latency. (2) Use AbarVa’s inventory view to list all bank relationships/accounts and tag critical vs. tail; phase connections so treasury gets 80% coverage fast, rather than boiling the ocean.
